RmlUi, vendored for VaCuusRml
=============================

upstream: https://github.com/mikke89/RmlUi
commit:   0ae381e00d7426762bb5ed897973366358b16642
vendored: 2026-07-29

VENDORED_SHA.txt NEXT TO THIS FILE HOLDS THAT SHA AND NOTHING ELSE, and must keep
holding nothing else: Tools/gen_rcss_matrix.py:34,134 reads the whole file and
.strip()s it into the generated docs/buyer/rcss-matrix.md header. This file is the
human half -- what is here, and the local patches. Read both before re-vendoring.

What is here, and why exactly this
----------------------------------
Vendored per docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-vacuus-m1-render-spike.md:114-122:

    cp -r Include Source Backends LICENSE.txt readme.md $DEST/
    rm -rf $DEST/Source/Lua $DEST/Source/SVG $DEST/Source/Lottie
    echo "<sha>" > $DEST/VENDORED_SHA.txt

Backends/ is reference material and is never compiled. Only Source/Core and
Source/Debugger are built, through the per-file relay .cpp files that
Source/VaCuusRml/Private/Gen/ generates.

Local patches
-------------
This tree was byte-identical to the upstream commit above until 2026-08-03.
Re-vendoring procedure: copy the file list above from the pinned commit, reapply
the patch(es) below, then run the verification named with each one -- a patch
that is silently lost re-introduces a defect nobody can see on screen.

Patch #1 -- data-style compares against the unit-less variant (bead VaCuus-akj.17).

Source/Core/DataViewDefault.cpp, DataViewStyle::Update. Upstream decides whether a
data-style binding needs re-applying by comparing the incoming string against
`p->Get<String>()`, and Property::Get<T> forwards straight to the property's value
Variant (Include/RmlUi/Core/Property.h:41-45), which does not carry the unit -- that
is a separate member (Property.h:50-51). So the property parsed out of "100px" reads
back as "100" and never compares equal to the string that produced it. Every dirty of
the bound variable therefore called Element::SetProperty with an unchanged value, and
SetProperty does not compare either (ElementStyle.cpp:606-618 -> PropertyDictionary
::SetProperty + DirtyProperty, unconditional), nor does ComputeValues, which returns
the DIRTY set rather than a changed-value set (ElementStyle.cpp:1022-1026). So the
element restyles, and a layout property relayouts the whole document, every time.

Whether that also costs a PUBLISHED frame depends on which property is bound, and the
first version of the test below got this wrong -- it bound `width`, and passed with
the patch reverted. Two RmlUi shortcuts absorb the layout-only path: an unchanged box
never reaches OnResize, and ElementText reuses its compiled geometry when the
regenerated mesh compares equal (ElementText.cpp:530-536). The border/background path
has no such check -- ElementBackgroundBorder::GenerateGeometry releases and re-makes
its mesh unconditionally (ElementBackgroundBorder.cpp:131-137) -- so a no-op write to
border-*-width, border-radius or box-shadow is a fresh handle plus resource traffic,
both legs of VaCuus's publish gate. A HUD whose model dirties a coarse top-level name
each tick (FVaCuusBoundModel::ApplyUpdate dirties the ROOT of a nested field) then
published EVERY frame while nothing on it changed: measured 100 of 100.

Not fixed at the VaCuus layer, because it cannot be: the plugin never sees this
call. Factory::RegisterDataViewInstancer refuses a duplicate name and logs a warning
(Source/Core/Factory.cpp:561-567), so "style" cannot be shadowed by our own view;
Element::SetProperty is not virtual (Include/RmlUi/Core/Element.h:177), so no custom
element instancer can intercept it; and DataModel::DirtyVariable takes top-level
names only, so the coarse dirty that exposes this cannot be narrowed either.

Verification: automation test VaCuus.Model.View.DataStyleIdle
(Source/VaCuusRender/Private/Tests/VaCuusDataStyleIdleTest.cpp) drives a real view
whose model dirties a sibling field every frame while the bound style values stay
"4px" (border-left-width) and "120px" (width), and asserts ZERO published frames over
100. Revert this hunk and it fails with exactly the numbers a re-vendor that dropped
the patch would produce:

  Expected 'and the unit-bearing data-style bindings published NOT ONE of them
  (akj.17)' to be 0, but it was 100.
  Expected 'the new values settle back to zero published frames' to be 0, but it
  was 20.

The hunk, ABRIDGED -- the in-file comment is long enough that reproducing it here
twice would be the thing that rots. One line changes:

--- a/Source/Core/DataViewDefault.cpp
+++ b/Source/Core/DataViewDefault.cpp
@@ bool DataViewStyle::Update(DataModel& model)
 	if (element && GetExpression().Run(expr_interface, variant))
 	{
 		const String value = variant.Get<String>();
 		const Property* p = element->GetLocalProperty(property_name);
-		if (!p || p->Get<String>() != value)
+		/* VaCuus patch #1 comment -- see the file for the full text */
+		if (!p || p->ToString() != value)
 		{
 			element->SetProperty(property_name, value);
 			result = true;
 		}
 	}

Property::ToString() re-appends the unit and maps a keyword back to its name
(Source/Core/Property.cpp:12-20 -> PropertyDefinition::GetValue,
Source/Core/PropertyDefinition.cpp:91-135), so the comparison is now against the
string that produced the property. It is a strict widening of the equal case: it can
only make MORE comparisons succeed, never fewer, because a property's ToString is
the string a re-parse would produce. Values whose ToString is not the authored
spelling still compare unequal exactly as they did before, and re-set exactly as
often: colours other than lowercase #rrggbb (TypeConverter.cpp:267-273 spells a
Colourb that way), shorthands (no local property exists under the shorthand's own
name), and spellings that "%.3f" with trimmed trailing zeros cannot reproduce
("120.50px"). Those residues are documented for buyers in docs/buyer/perf-guide.md.

NOT yet offered upstream -- that is a maintainer action and nobody has taken it.
It should be: the hunk is upstream-shaped on purpose, and until it lands there
every re-vendor has to carry it by hand.


Patch #2 -- dll-interface removed from four HEADER-ONLY CLASS TEMPLATES (Win64 pass,
2026-08-03). Found by the plugin's first Windows build ever; invisible on Linux and
macOS by construction.

    Include/RmlUi/Core/ObserverPtr.h:42            class RMLUICORE_API ObserverPtr
    Include/RmlUi/Core/ObserverPtr.h:113           class RMLUICORE_API EnableObserverPtr
    Include/RmlUi/Core/UniqueRenderResource.h:14   class RMLUICORE_API UniqueRenderResource
    Include/RmlUi/Core/Traits.h:35                 class RMLUICORE_API Releaser

In each, `class RMLUICORE_API X` becomes `class X`. Nothing else changes.

THE MECHANISM. Include/RmlUi/Core/Header.h:8-21: in a shared build on Win32,
RMLUICORE_API is __declspec(dllexport) while compiling the library (RMLUI_CORE_EXPORTS
is set for VaCuusRml) and __declspec(dllimport) for everyone else. On a CLASS TEMPLATE
that is a category error. dllimport tells MSVC the members of every instantiation live
in another DLL, so a consumer TU stops instantiating them locally and emits __imp_
references instead -- which resolve only if the library happened to instantiate and
export that exact specialization. VaCuusJs asks for one the library never used:

    VaCuusJsDom.cpp.obj : error LNK2019: unresolved external symbol
    "__declspec(dllimport) public: __cdecl Rml::ObserverPtr<class Rml::Element>::
    ObserverPtr<class Rml::Element>(void)" (__imp_??0?$ObserverPtr@VElement@Rml@@@Rml@@QEAA@XZ)
    referenced in function "public: struct JSValue __cdecl
    FVaCuusJsViewContext::WrapElement(class Rml::Element *)"

Rml::Element is used constantly, but nothing inside RmlUi's own Core ever
default-constructs an ObserverPtr<Element>, so that one constructor was never emitted
into UnrealEditor-VaCuusRml.dll and never exported.

WHY REMOVING IT IS CORRECT RATHER THAN A WORKAROUND. All four templates are entirely
header-inline: no .cpp in Source/ defines a member of any of them, and the library
contains no explicit instantiation of any of them (both checked). A header-only
template needs no dll-interface at all -- every module compiles its own copy, which is
the normal C++ model. The non-template API those copies call IS still exported and
still carries the macro: ObserverPtrBlock plus AllocateObserverPtrBlock and
DeallocateObserverPtrBlockIfEmpty (ObserverPtr.h:10-15). The observer STATE therefore
stays single-instance in VaCuusRml.dll, which is the property that actually matters;
only the inline code around it is duplicated per module.

Off Windows the macro expands to __attribute__((visibility("default")))
(Header.h:45), which on a header-only template only widens symbol visibility for code
each module already instantiates for itself. That is why Linux and macOS linked
happily for six milestones with the defect present, and it is also why removing it
cannot change their behaviour: no cross-module reference to these inline members
exists on any platform.

VERIFICATION (the re-vendoring check for this patch): build any Win64 MODULAR target
-- e.g. `Build.bat <Project>Editor Win64 Development -project=...`. With the patch
reverted, UnrealEditor-VaCuusJs.dll fails to link with the LNK2019 above. With it
applied, all five plugin DLLs link. Seen both ways on 2026-08-03. A monolithic Win64
target does NOT exercise this: VaCuusRml.Build.cs defines RMLUI_STATIC_LIB there, and
Header.h:51 then makes RMLUICORE_API empty, so the defect cannot appear.

NOT yet offered upstream -- same standing as patch #1. It should be; the fix is
upstream-shaped and costs upstream nothing.


Patch #3 -- box-shadow renders an opaque white rectangle and republishes every frame
when SaveLayerAsTexture is not implemented (beads VaCuus-u0q, VaCuus-iuv).

Three files, four hunks. This is one fix; carrying any hunk without the others is worse
than carrying none, and the middle paragraph below says exactly why.

  Include/RmlUi/Core/CallbackTexture.h   CallbackTextureInterface::SaveLayerAsTexture
  Source/Core/CallbackTexture.cpp        same, definition
  Source/Core/GeometryBoxShadow.cpp      the texture callback's return
  Source/Core/ElementBackgroundBorder.cpp  GenerateGeometry

THE DEFECT IS UPSTREAM'S, not ours, and it fires for ANY backend that leaves
SaveLayerAsTexture at its optional default -- which the base class explicitly permits by
returning a zero handle (Source/Core/RenderInterface.cpp:37-40). Two things then go wrong
at once, and the second one hides behind the first:

  (a) THE WHITE RECTANGLE. ElementBackgroundBorder::GenerateGeometry commits to the
      box-shadow path on `computed.has_box_shadow()` alone: it ERASES the element's normal
      background and border and stores a BoxShadowRenderable instead. Render() then draws
      that renderable's `geometry` -- a premultiplied WHITE quad covering the border box
      extended by 1.5*blur+spread (Source/Core/BoxShadowCache.cpp:56-59) -- textured with
      the null handle. VaCuus's replayer binds GWhiteTexture and clears bUseTexture for
      handle 0 (VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:506-512), so the quad comes out as pure vertex
      colour: an opaque white box where the element's own background and border should be.

  (b) THE FRAME-RATE CHURN. The texture callback returns true whether or not it produced
      a handle (Source/Core/GeometryBoxShadow.cpp, the old `return true` after
      SaveLayerAsTexture), so CallbackTextureDatabase::EnsureLoaded sees neither a handle
      nor load_failed and re-runs the WHOLE callback on every frame that asks for the
      texture (Source/Core/TextureDatabase.cpp:46-60): a layer pushed, a blur filter
      compiled and released, geometry made and released. That is permanent resource
      traffic, which permanently trips FVaCuusCommandBuffer::HasResourceTraffic() and
      forces a published frame every tick on a document that never changes.

THE HUNKS.

1. CallbackTextureInterface::SaveLayerAsTexture returns bool instead of void -- true only
   when a texture handle was really produced. Purely additive (an ignored return still
   compiles), and upstream-shaped: its sibling GenerateTexture already returns bool with
   the same meaning, and CallbackTextureFunction's own doc comment promises "@return True
   on success" (CallbackTexture.h:19), which the box-shadow callback could not honour
   without this.

2. GeometryBoxShadow's callback returns that bool instead of an unconditional true. Fixes
   (b): one failure latches load_failed and the callback never runs again for that cache
   entry.

3. ElementBackgroundBorder::GenerateGeometry PROBES the shadow texture (Texture::
   GetDimensions, which is what forces the callback) and falls through to the ordinary
   background/border path when no texture was produced. Fixes (a).

   It deliberately does NOT render BoxShadowRenderable::background_border_geometry, which
   looks like the obvious substitute: BoxShadowCache::GetHandle premultiplies that mesh's
   colours WITHOUT opacity (BoxShadowCache.cpp:85-91, opacity instead going into the shadow
   quad's vertex alpha at :57-58), so at opacity < 1 it would render fully opaque. The
   normal path premultiplies by opacity and is exactly right.

4. THE REFUSED RENDERABLE IS PARKED on the ordinary background instead of being dropped.
   THIS IS THE HUNK THAT LOOKS LIKE BOOKKEEPING AND IS NOT -- the first version of this
   patch omitted it and was caught by its own test. BoxShadowCache holds entries by WeakPtr
   and erases the entry from the renderable's destructor (BoxShadowCache.cpp:13, :65-77),
   so letting the SharedPtr die at the end of GenerateGeometry destroys the cache entry and
   with it the CallbackTexture whose load_failed hunk 2 just set. Every subsequent restyle
   then minted a fresh entry and re-ran the whole callback -- (b) again, gated on restyle
   instead of on frame. Measured: 70 refusals across 70 restyled frames, versus 1.

WHY THIS IS NOT FIXED AT THE VaCuus LAYER, checked rather than assumed. The obvious move
is to refuse the PROPERTY, so `has_box_shadow()` is never true. It cannot be done:
StyleSheetSpecification::RegisterParser REFUSES to overwrite an existing name -- it logs
"Parser with name %s already exists!" and returns false (StyleSheetSpecification.cpp:99-110)
-- so the registered "box_shadow" parser (:245) cannot be shadowed by one of ours. There is
no capability query on RenderInterface to add either without breaking the reference
backends, which override SaveLayerAsTexture but would not override a new predicate.

WHAT THE PLUGIN CONTRIBUTES, and it must land with these hunks: the recorder now OVERRIDES
both layer-capture virtuals rather than inheriting them, returning 0 with one latched
Warning per view that names the property, the reason and the substitute
(VaCuusRecordingRenderInterface.cpp, SaveLayerAsTexture/SaveLayerAsMaskImage). Without
hunks 3 and 4 that return value is destructive; without the override the failure is silent.

VERIFICATION (the re-vendoring check): automation tests
VaCuus.Render.LayerCapture.Refused and VaCuus.Render.LayerCapture.RestyleChurn
(Source/VaCuusRender/Private/Tests/VaCuusLayerCaptureTest.cpp). Each hunk has been reverted
alone and watched to fail:

  - hunks 2+3 reverted (the true pre-fix state): Refused never settles --
    "still publishing after 200 frames (201 published, 201 recorded)".
  - hunk 3 reverted alone: "Expected 'and draws no opaque-white quad ...' to be 0, but it
    was 12" (three shadowed elements, four corners each).
  - hunk 2 reverted alone: RestyleChurn reports "to be 10, but it was 70" -- one refusal
    per restyled frame. NOTE that Refused still PASSES in this state, which is not what one
    would guess: once hunk 3 declines the shadow path, an idle document never asks for the
    texture again. That is exactly why RestyleChurn exists.
  - hunk 4 omitted: same 10 -> 70 as above.

MASK-IMAGE IS NOT FIXED HERE, only made loud (bead VaCuus-iuv). SaveLayerAsMaskImage needs
the same layer capture, and there is nothing to make harmless short of implementing it: the
mask decorators are drawn BEFORE the capture (Source/Core/ElementEffects.cpp:300-305), so
with layers skipped at replay the mask artwork lands in the frame and paints over the
element. Verified on screen, not inferred.

NOT yet offered upstream -- same standing as patches #1 and #2. Hunks 1-3 are
upstream-shaped and fix a real upstream defect for any optional-feature-skipping backend;
hunk 4 is a lifetime consequence of hunk 3 and travels with it.


Patch #4 -- a `transition` whose value contains var() never runs, and says nothing
(bead VaCuus-6gj).

One file, one hunk: Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp, ElementStyle::TransitionPropertyChanges.

THE DEFECT IS UPSTREAM'S and it is silent in the strongest sense -- no warning, no error,
no log line anywhere, in a debug build, at any log level. A property value containing var()
is stored UNPARSED as Property{value, Unit::VAR_EXPRESSION} (Source/Core/
PropertySpecification.cpp:260-267) and resolved at COMPUTE time (ElementStyle.cpp:277-315).
That is deliberate and correct, and it is exactly why var() works everywhere else. But
TransitionPropertyChanges reads `transition` EARLY, on purpose -- "We get the local property
directly here to intercept property changes even before the computed values are ready"
(:388) -- and then tested `transition_property->value.GetType() != Variant::TRANSITIONLIST`
and returned. A VAR_EXPRESSION is a String variant, so it returned, and the whole
declaration was gone.

The blast radius is the obvious authoring idiom: RCSS has no calc(), so var() is the only
theming layer the matrix can recommend, and timing tokens in custom properties are the first
thing anyone does with it. In the 2d6 demo that was ~30 transitions across four component
batches, three screens and a screenshot-reviewed component catalogue, none of which had ever
run, for days, because the symptom is "the element snaps".

`animation` IS NOT AFFECTED and needs no patch, contrary to the original bug report. It is
read through ComputedValues::animation(), which goes via GetLocalPropertyWithResolvedVariables
and therefore resolves (Source/Core/ComputedValues.cpp:8-16). Measured, not assumed: with this
patch fully reverted, the test's #anim-variable element still animates.

THE HUNK is a PURE INSERTION -- `git diff` on the file reports 36 insertions and zero
deletions, deliberately, so a re-vendor can paste it back between the null check and the
TRANSITIONLIST test without touching an upstream line:

    const Property* transition_property = GetLocalProperty(PropertyId::Transition, sources.inline_properties, new_definition);
    if (!transition_property)
        return;
+   /* the full comment is in the file; not repeated here, twice is what rots */
+   Property transition_property_storage;
+   if (transition_property->unit == Unit::VAR_EXPRESSION)
+   {
+       const PropertySources transition_sources{sources.element, new_definition, sources.inline_properties};
+       std::optional<PropertyDictionary> transition_substituted_shorthands;
+       SmallUnorderedSet<String> transition_variable_dependencies;
+       transition_property = ResolveVariablesWithShorthandExpansion(transition_sources, PropertyId::Transition,
+           transition_property, transition_substituted_shorthands, transition_variable_dependencies,
+           transition_property_storage);
+       if (!transition_property)
+           return;
+   }
    if (transition_property->value.GetType() != Variant::TRANSITIONLIST)
        return;

`transition_property_storage` is what the TransitionList reference two lines down borrows,
so it must stay at function scope; the set and the optional are block-local on purpose, so
that a `transition` with no var() in it constructs neither.

WHY THIS IS SAFE HERE SPECIFICALLY, opened rather than assumed. The worry with resolving
anything at this point is compute ordering, and upstream has already answered it: the
substitution path names THIS FUNCTION as the case it is written for -- "We cannot always use
the definition or inline properties from the style of the property element. Particularly in
TransitionPropertyChanges, these are not yet set for the current element" (:227-230) -- and
this same function already calls the same helper on every transitioned property's start and
target value a few lines below (:410-414 before the patch). The sources passed here match
the lookup exactly: the element's current inline properties against the NEW definition, so a
custom property redeclared by the same rule that changed the transition resolves against the
state being transitioned TO. `transition` is a plain property, not a shorthand
(StyleSheetSpecification.cpp:399, and no RegisterShorthand under that name), so the
shorthand-expansion leg of the helper is never taken; it is used anyway because it is the
call the neighbouring lines make. A nullptr return means substitution failed, and
SubstituteVariables / ResolveVariables have already logged which variable or which value
(:212-217, :308-312) -- so the remaining failure mode is loud, which the original never was.
Cost is zero unless the property really is a VAR_EXPRESSION.

WHY THIS IS NOT FIXED AT THE VaCuus LAYER: the plugin never sees this call. TransitionProperty-
Changes is private to ElementStyle, `transition` cannot be re-registered over
(StyleSheetSpecification::RegisterParser refuses a duplicate name, :99-110), and there is no
element hook between the definition change and the early read. A VaCuus-side WARNING was
considered as the fallback deliverable and rejected once the fix landed: after this patch the
`!= TRANSITIONLIST` branch is unreachable for a var() value, so the warning would be dead
code, and the branch it would guard lives in this same function -- a re-vendor that lost the
patch would lose the warning with it. The automation test below is the guard instead.

VERIFICATION (the re-vendoring check): automation test VaCuus.Core.Style.TransitionVariable
(Source/VaCuus/Private/Tests/VaCuusStyleVariableTest.cpp). Reverted and watched to fail on
2026-08-06:

  #variable, transition with var() in its duration STARTS rather than snapping (6gj):
    expected opacity 1.0000 (±0.0100), got 0.2500
  #variable, var(--slow) = 20s, has barely moved after 250 ms:
    expected opacity 0.9500 (±0.0600), got 0.2500

with every control still passing -- including "#anim-variable, animation with var() runs too
-- it was NEVER the broken half (6gj): opacity 0.2500", which is what keeps a future reader
from patching the animation path as well.

NOT yet offered upstream -- same standing as patches #1-#3. This one is the most
upstream-shaped of the four: it uses upstream's own helper, in the function upstream's own
comment says that helper was written for.
